_about: Hand-researched 2027 prospect scouting profiles, synthesized from public reporting (Nov 2026). Keyed by FBGM pid. Refresh stats2025 -> the 2026 season after it ends. Read by scripts/build_mock_draft.py into public/mock/scout-2027.json.

12591.name: Jeremiah Smith
12591.summary: Big, physically dominant X receiver who has been the most productive wideout in college football since arriving as a true freshman. Widely viewed as the top overall prospect in the 2027 class and a near-lock top-five pick.
strengths: Rare size-speed blend for a perimeter receiver
Wins contested catches and creates after the catch
Elite, consistent production from day one
weaknesses: Few clear flaws noted; missed parts of two 2025 games
Will face scrutiny on route nuance versus press at next level
12591.honors: 2025 Unanimous All-American; 2x Big Ten Receiver of the Year (2024, 2025)
12591.notes: Already Ohio State's career leader in receptions, receiving yards and receiving TDs during 2026.

12554.name: Colin Simmons
12554.summary: Explosive speed-rush edge defender and arguably the best front-seven player in the 2027 class. Led the SEC in sacks in 2025 and projects as a top-10 pick if his frame holds up.
strengths: Explosive first step and ability to bend the edge
Elite pass-rush production and pressure volume
Forces fumbles; disruptive finisher
weaknesses: Light for an every-down NFL edge (around 240 lbs)
Run-defense anchor questioned versus bigger tackles
12554.notes: Had 5.5 sacks vs. Tennessee in 2026 (tied SEC single-game record). Hurt vs. Florida in Week 7 of 2026 and missed the next game.

12424.name: Dylan Stewart
12424.summary: Long, twitchy edge rusher with top-10 tools whose sack production has lagged his talent. Still a likely first-rounder, but 2026 has been interrupted by a back injury and a suspension.
strengths: Long, wiry frame with burst and flexibility
Disruptive beyond the box score; strip-sack ability
High ceiling as a double-digit-sack NFL rusher
12424.notes: Preseason back injury in 2026, then suspended indefinitely after an on-field incident vs. Alabama (Week 4). Returned in Week 6 vs. Florida with two forced fumbles.

12483.name: Julian Sayin
12483.summary: Accurate, efficient pocket passer who led the nation's top-graded QB play in his first year as a starter. His accuracy and ball security give him first-round appeal; size and mobility are the debate.
strengths: Elite accuracy; completed 77% of passes in 2025
Protects the football with very low turnover-worthy play rate
Poised, quick processor from the pocket
weaknesses: Undersized frame for an NFL starter
12483.honors: 2025 Big Ten Freshman of the Year; 2025 Second-team All-Big Ten; 4th in 2025 Heisman voting
12483.notes: Began at Alabama, transferred to Ohio State in January 2024 after Nick Saban retired. Redshirt-eligible for 2027 draft; could return.

12338.name: Arch Manning
12338.summary: Prototype-sized quarterback with genuine athleticism who improved over the back half of 2025. Ranked near the top of most 2027 boards on traits, though evaluators want more week-to-week consistency.
strengths: Ideal NFL size and arm
Legitimate dual-threat; 10 rushing TDs in 2025
Improved steadily as a first-year starter
12338.notes: Led Texas to an early 2026 win over No. 1 Ohio State.

12621.name: Jordan Seaton
12621.summary: Former five-star left tackle who started from day one at Colorado and was the top OT in the 2026 transfer portal. Strong pass protector projected as a first-round tackle.
strengths: Polished pass protection; allowed no sacks in 2025
Two-year starter at left tackle since true freshman
Athletic, high-pedigree blindside blocker
weaknesses: Run-blocking grades lag his pass pro
Missed final three games of 2025 with injury
12621.notes: Transferred from Colorado to LSU in January 2026.

12629.name: David Stone
12629.summary: Former elite recruit at defensive tackle who broke out as a run defender in 2025. Scheme-versatile interior lineman with first-round projection, though pass-rush production is modest.
strengths: Can play 1-technique or 3-technique
Strong anchor and run awareness
Gets hands up; batted several passes in 2025
12629.notes: Suffered a practice injury in September 2026.

12639.name: CJ Carr
12639.summary: Quick-release pocket passer with strong leadership traits who won the Notre Dame job in 2025. Has a strong TD-to-INT profile and is a first-round candidate if he declares early.
strengths: Gets the ball out quickly
Excellent TD-to-INT ratio
Natural leader; wins games (10-2 as 2025 starter)
weaknesses: Could return to school rather than declare
12639.notes: Redshirted 2024 recovering from an elbow injury. Eligible for 2027 but may stay in school.

12416.name: Charlie Becker
12416.summary: Vertical receiver who broke out late in 2025, starring in Indiana's Big Ten title and national championship run. A projected Day 1-2 pick whose stock rides on a bigger 2026 target share.
strengths: Big-play threat; 20.0 yards per catch led Big Ten
Strong contested-catch ability
Rose to the moment in playoff games
weaknesses: Lost his QB and top WRs from title team
12416.honors: 2025 CFP national champion; 2026 AP Preseason Second-team All-American

12594.name: Isaac Brown
12594.summary: Compact, explosive runner who has averaged nearly 8 yards per carry in his career. A productive tailback whose draft range depends on size and durability.
strengths: Explosive home-run speed (8.8 ypc in 2025)
Elusive with good contact balance
Proven early producer; 1,000-yard true freshman
weaknesses: Missed late 2025 with a leg injury
12594.honors: 2025 Third-team All-ACC; 2024 ACC Rookie of the Year
12594.notes: Leg injury at Virginia Tech (Nov. 1, 2025) ended his regular season. Briefly entered the portal, then stayed at Louisville.

12609.name: Darian Mensah
12609.summary: Productive, well-traveled passer now at his third school in three seasons. Put up big numbers at Duke and has been red-hot at Miami in 2026, but ball security under pressure is a concern.
strengths: Strong TD-to-INT production two straight years
Accurate; over 80% completions early in 2026
Proven multi-system starter
weaknesses: Fumbling issues (16 in 27 games per PFF)
12609.notes: Tulane (2023-24) to Duke (2025) to Miami (2026); Duke sued over his January 2026 portal exit before settling.

12725.name: Matayo Uiagalelei
12725.summary: Powerful edge defender on one of the nation's deepest fronts. Productive pass rusher across two seasons; projects as a Day 1-2 edge.
strengths: Consistent pressure producer (52 pressures in 2025)
Strength to set the edge in run game
Forces fumbles and finishes

12616.name: KJ Bolden
12616.summary: Instinctive, versatile safety who can play deep or slide into the slot. A sure tackler with high football IQ and a strong candidate for the first round.
strengths: Reliable tackler with very low miss rate
Nickel/safety versatility
High football IQ

12618.name: Anthonie Knapp
12618.summary: Two-year starting left tackle who moved to left guard for 2026. Settled in after a rough start to 2025 and many evaluators view his NFL future inside.
strengths: Extensive starting experience at left tackle
Improved pass protection as 2025 progressed
Positional flexibility at tackle or guard
weaknesses: May lack length/athleticism to stay at tackle
12618.notes: Shifted from left tackle to left guard for the 2026 season.

12544.name: Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa
12544.summary: Physical, downhill linebacker who graded as the best run defender in college football in 2025. Also effective as a blitzer and in coverage, but his sample is small and injuries are a concern.
strengths: Elite run defense and tackling in the box
Effective blitzer; 3 sacks in 2025
Held up well in coverage
12544.notes: Tore an ACL before the 2024 season; suffered a season-ending knee injury vs. Syracuse in November 2025.

12625.name: Ryan Williams
12625.summary: Explosive, young slot/outside receiver who starred as a 17-year-old freshman before a quieter 2025. Rebounding in 2026 and still carries first-round upside.
strengths: Explosive big-play speed
Dangerous after the catch
Production at an extremely young age
12625.notes: Changed his surname to Coleman-Williams in March 2026; may appear as Ryan Coleman-Williams on boards.

12462.name: John Henry Daley
12462.summary: High-motor edge rusher who exploded for 11.5 sacks at Utah in 2025 and followed Kyle Whittingham to Michigan. Elite pressure rate, but he is older and coming off a ruptured Achilles.
strengths: Elite pressure and win rates in 2025
Relentless motor and hand usage
Returned strong in 2026 after major injury
weaknesses: Older prospect after a two-year mission
12462.notes: BYU (2023) to Utah (2024-25) to Michigan (2026). Ruptured Achilles vs. Kansas State on Nov. 22, 2025; back for 2026 and earned a Big Ten Defensive Player of the Week.

12583.name: Bryant Wesco Jr.
12583.summary: Long, vertical receiver who is among the ACC's most dangerous deep threats when healthy. Injuries have limited his volume, putting him in the Day 2 range.
strengths: Career average above 17 yards per catch
Long strider who stretches the field
Red-zone scorer (6 TD in 7 games)
weaknesses: Durability; 2025 ended early with back injury
12583.notes: Season-ending back injury after the SMU game in October 2025; medically cleared for 2026.

12608.name: Jayden Jackson
12608.summary: Big-bodied interior lineman who pairs with David Stone on Oklahoma's front. Disruptive when healthy but modest box-score production so far; a mid-round type pending a 2026 jump.
strengths: Mass and power to anchor inside
Disruptive penetrator when healthy
Starting experience since freshman year

12579.name: Koi Perich
12579.summary: Versatile ball-hawking safety who also returns punts and has taken offensive snaps. Transferred from Minnesota to Oregon for 2026 after a less productive sophomore season.
strengths: Ball skills; 5 INT as a freshman
Multi-phase value on special teams and offense
High-volume tackler (82 in 2025)
weaknesses: Needs to prove consistency at new program
12579.honors: 2024 Second-team All-American; 2024 First-team All-Big Ten; 2025 Second-team All-Big Ten
12579.notes: Transferred from Minnesota to Oregon in January 2026.

12637.name: Zabien Brown
12637.summary: Long, high-pedigree outside corner with big-play instincts, including two pick-sixes in 2025. Has first-round tools but needs more snap-to-snap consistency.
strengths: Ideal size and length for boundary corner
Playmaker with the ball in the air
Turns turnovers into points
12637.stats2025: 39 tkl, 2.5 TFL, 2 INT (2 TD), 6 PD, 1 FF
12637.notes: 99-yard pick-six vs. Tennessee and a pick-six vs. Oklahoma in the CFP in 2025.

12605.name: Sammy Brown
12605.summary: Instinctive, athletic off-ball linebacker who has led Clemson in tackles and excels against the run. A Day 2 type with starter traits.
strengths: Elite run-stop production
Top-end speed for the position
Effective blitzer with double-digit career sacks
12605.honors: 2025 First-team All-ACC; 2025 Blanchard-Rogers Trophy; 2024 ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year

12634.name: Trey'Dez Green
12634.summary: Huge, athletic receiving tight end and two-sport athlete who set LSU's tight end TD record in 2025. A red-zone mismatch with Day 1-2 upside if his hands become more reliable.
strengths: Rare size and athleticism at 6-7
Red-zone weapon; 7 TD in 2025
Basketball background shows in body control
12634.notes: Also played on LSU's men's basketball team.

12486.name: Will Echoles
12486.summary: Converted edge who became a disruptive interior defensive tackle and anchor of the Ole Miss line. Led Power Four interior linemen in pressures in 2025; first-round candidate.
strengths: Elite interior pressure production
Edge-like quickness inside
Durable; started all 15 games in 2025
weaknesses: Sack totals modest relative to pressures
Still refining technique after position change

12571.name: Xavier Atkins
12571.summary: Undersized, explosive linebacker who broke out as a blitzing playmaker for Auburn in 2025. Productive, but his draft status is clouded by his 2026 dismissal from the program.
strengths: Explosive blitzer; 9 sacks in 2025
Big tackle-for-loss production
Fast, aggressive downhill player
12571.notes: LSU transfer (2024). Reported dismissed from Auburn five games into 2026 (October 2026); reason and next destination not confirmed.

12515.name: Boo Carter
12515.summary: Twitchy, athletic defensive back and former Tennessee Mr. Football who flashed as a freshman starter. Talent is real, but his release from Tennessee raises character and commitment questions.
strengths: Plus athlete with playmaking instincts
Started as a true freshman in the SEC
Multi-role value on defense and returns
12515.notes: Released by Tennessee on Nov. 16, 2025 after team-standards issues; now at Colorado for 2026.

12574.name: Adon Shuler
12574.summary: Veteran three-year starting safety and vocal leader of Notre Dame's secondary. Brings ball production and blitz value, but tackling consistency is a knock.
strengths: Ball skills; 6 career INT
Effective blitzer off the edge
Experienced leader in the secondary
12574.stats2025: 12 G · 53 tkl, 1 sack, 2 INT, 5 PD, 2 FF

12595.name: KJ Duff
12595.summary: Towering outside receiver who dominates at the catch point and had a 1,000-yard season in 2025. Hot start to 2026 has him climbing toward the first round.
strengths: Rare 6-6 size on the perimeter
Led FBS in contested catches in 2025
Big-play producer (18.1 ypc in 2025)

12668.name: LaNorris Sellers
12668.summary: Big, physical dual-threat quarterback once viewed as a potential top pick. Regressed in 2025 behind a struggling team; his running gives him a floor but processing must improve.
strengths: Rare size and strength for a QB
Dangerous runner, especially in 2026
Strong arm; 8.3 yards per attempt in 2025
weaknesses: Slow processing; holds the ball too long

12576.name: Charles Jagusah
12576.summary: Massive, former blue-chip offensive tackle who has rarely been healthy. Started the 2024 national title game, but missed all of 2025, leaving his projection largely on traits.
strengths: Huge frame at about 6-6, 330-plus
Played left tackle in CFP title game
High recruiting pedigree
12576.notes: Tore right pectoral before 2024; fractured left humerus in a UTV accident and missed all of 2025 and the start of 2026. Eligibility year may be a redshirt year.

12530.name: OJ Frederique Jr.
12530.summary: Man-cover outside corner who broke out as a freshman starter in 2024 and has been viewed as one of the better 2027 corners. His stock now hinges on health after a significant injury in the 2026 opener.
strengths: Patient, disciplined footwork in man coverage
Consistent pass breakups (7 in each of 2024 and 2025)
Starting experience on a playoff-level defense
weaknesses: Limited ball production: one career interception
Missed time to injuries in both 2025 and 2026
Slender frame for an outside corner
12530.notes: Coach Mario Cristobal said in early September 2026 that he suffered a significant injury after Week 1 and would be out for an extended period. Missed the 2025 CFP semifinal with an injury. Listed at 6-0, 185-195.

12676.name: Byrum Brown
12676.summary: Big, powerful dual-threat quarterback who followed coach Alex Golesh from USF to Auburn for his final season. Elite college production as a runner and passer, but evaluators view him as a developmental, later-round arm.
strengths: Physical, productive runner with 1,000-yard rushing ability
Prolific touchdown producer: 42 total TDs in 2025
Sturdy 6-3, 230-plus frame
weaknesses: Throwing mechanics draw criticism from evaluators
Most production came against Group of Five competition
Missed most of 2024 with a lower-leg injury
12676.stats2025: 12 G · 3,158 pass yds, 28 TD, 7 INT; 1,008 rush yds, 14 TD
12676.notes: Transferred from South Florida to Auburn for 2026. Set roughly 15 USF school records. PFF's page lists draft eligibility as 2028, which looks inconsistent with his senior status.

12567.name: Ellis Robinson IV
12567.summary: Former No. 1 cornerback recruit in the 2024 class who became a ball-hawking starter for Georgia in 2025. Has the tools of a plus NFL corner but needs refinement and added strength.
strengths: Fluid hips and quick turns to carry receivers vertically
Strong ball production: 4 INTs in 2025
Willing, aggressive tackler
weaknesses: Thin frame; can be pushed around in space
Gambles in coverage, allowing big plays (21 yds per catch)
12567.notes: Sources differ on class (junior vs. redshirt sophomore). Listed 6-0, 180.

12627.name: T.J. Moore
12627.summary: Tall, smooth route-running receiver who has started since his freshman year and led Clemson in receiving yards in 2025. Viewed as a potential first-round pick, though his 2026 production in a deep WR class is key.
strengths: Refined route runner who separates out of breaks
Reliable hands and concentration
Can align in multiple spots; gains yards after catch
weaknesses: More smooth than explosive; limited vertical burst
Needs to add weight to his frame

12415.name: Mario Craver
12415.summary: Undersized speed receiver who transferred from Mississippi State and became Texas A&M's top big-play threat in 2025. Projects as a Day 2-3 slot/gadget weapon whose size is the main question.
strengths: Elite top-end speed to stretch defenses
Breaks tackles and creates after the catch on screens
Versatile: slot, outside, jet motion, backfield
weaknesses: Very small frame (about 5-9, 165) raises durability concerns

12601.name: Ahmad Hardy
12601.summary: Powerful, balanced one-cut runner who led the SEC in rushing in 2025 after transferring from Louisiana-Monroe. Was shot in the leg in May 2026 and only made his season debut on Oct. 31.
strengths: Elite contact balance; consistently falls forward
Sharp one-cut and lateral agility
Patient runner who breaks arm tackles
weaknesses: Lacks long speed to finish breakaways
12601.honors: 2025 consensus All-American; Doak Walker Award finalist
12601.notes: Transferred from Louisiana-Monroe (1,351 rush yds in 2024). Wounded in a May 2026 shooting; returned to game action vs. Arkansas on Oct. 31, 2026. Jeanty comparison attributed to ESPN's Matt Miller.

12611.name: Kewan Lacy
12611.summary: Elusive, high-volume back who set Ole Miss single-season rushing records in 2025 after transferring from Missouri. Regarded among the top RBs in the 2027 class, with some first-round chatter.
strengths: Elusive with home-run ability
Excellent vision, instincts and quickness
Contributes as receiver and pass protector
12611.notes: Transferred from Missouri. draft sites list him around 200-205 lbs.

12531.name: Nick Marsh
12531.summary: Big, fast outside receiver who was Michigan State's focal point before transferring to Indiana for 2026, where he has produced at a high clip. Ranked near the top of the 2027 WR class.
strengths: Prototypical 6-3, 210-plus frame
Reported 4.3-range speed
Commanded defensive game plans as MSU's top target
weaknesses: Needs more strength at the catch point
12531.notes: Transferred from Michigan State to Indiana in January 2026.

12565.name: Dorian Fleming
12565.summary: Receiving-oriented tight end who transferred from Georgia State and became a high-volume target for Maryland in 2025. Projects as a move/receiving TE prospect; draft-board coverage is thin.
strengths: Moves well with fluid hips in routes
Sound route mechanics and footwork
High-volume target (40 catches in 2025)
weaknesses: Best paired with a blocking tight end
12565.honors: 2026 preseason second-team All-Big Ten (Pro Football Network)
12565.notes: Transferred from Georgia State (49 rec, 558 yds, 6 TD in 2024). Listed 6-3, 245.

12722.name: Sam Leavitt
12722.summary: Mobile, improvisational quarterback who led Arizona State to a Big 12 title in 2024 before a foot injury cut short his 2025. Transferred to LSU for 2026; currently viewed as a Day 3 prospect with upside.
strengths: Extends plays and creates outside structure
Quick release; throws well on the run and off-platform
Productive runner
weaknesses: Bails from clean pockets; holds ball too long
12722.stats2025: 7 G · 145 comp, 1,628 yds, 10 TD; 306 rush yds, 5 TD
12722.honors: 2024 Big 12 Offensive Freshman of the Year; 2024 second-team All-Big 12
12722.notes: Michigan State (2023) to Arizona State (2024-25) to LSU (2026). 2025 season ended with foot surgery after the Sept. 20 Baylor game.

12435.name: Ashton Hamtpon
12435.summary: Long, physical press-man corner who has developed into one of the top-rated cornerbacks for 2027. Several analysts slot him in the first round, and he has graded well in 2026.
strengths: Rare size (about 6-3, 205) for press coverage
Explosive and physical at the line
High 2026 coverage grades from PFF

12699.name: AJ Harris
12699.summary: Former five-star corner (Georgia, then Penn State) once tipped as a 2026 first-rounder whose stock slid after a down 2025. Transferred to Indiana for a final-year rebound; projects in the Day 2-3 range.
strengths: Ideal NFL frame with strength to press
Short-area quickness and fluidity for his size
Contributes in run support and on special teams
12699.notes: Georgia to Penn State to Indiana (2026). sources list about 190.

12582.name: Ryan Wingo
12582.summary: Big, fast vertical receiver for Texas who produces big plays in bursts. Grades in the second-round range, with route polish and hands the main development points.
strengths: 4.3-range speed; tracks the deep ball well
Strong body control at the catch point
Dangerous with the ball after the catch
weaknesses: Drops: seven in the 2025 regular season
12582.notes: Listed with a shoulder injury on Rotowire's 2026 page. Sources differ on class (sophomore vs. junior).

12481.name: Jamarious Brown
12481.summary: Stout interior defensive tackle and rotational contributor on Ole Miss's 2025 playoff defense. Limited draft-specific coverage found.
strengths: Heavy 315-pound interior body
Early contributor; freshman All-American in 2024
Versatile high school background (edge, DT, RB)
weaknesses: Low tackle volume for a starter-level prospect
12481.notes: No 2027 draft scouting report or ranking found. Sources disagree on class (sophomore vs. junior).

12669.name: Quincy Rhodes Jr.
12669.summary: Long, prototypical defensive end who broke out in 2025 with 8 sacks and 15.5 TFL. Projections range from Day 2 to first round.
strengths: Rare 6-6, 270-plus frame and length
Effective bull rush and spin move
Sets the edge against the run
weaknesses: Only one productive season on his resume
12669.notes: sources list him about 6-6, 273-276. He is an edge/DE, not an interior DL.

12557.name: Yhonzae Pierre
12557.summary: Power-based edge rusher who emerged in 2025 as Alabama's top pass rusher. Several boards rank him among the top three edges in the 2027 class, with a Round 1-2 projection.
strengths: Strong bull rush and speed-to-power
Disruptive behind the line (14.5 TFL in 2025)
Forces turnovers (3 forced fumbles in 2025)
weaknesses: Pressure rate trails his sack totals
Pad level rises late in longer rushes
12557.notes: Sack totals differ by source (8 vs. 9). Listed about 6-3, 244.

12659.name: A'Mauri Washington
12659.summary: Massive, unusually athletic interior defensive lineman who returned to Oregon for 2026. Viewed as a possible first-rounder on traits, though his pass-rush production lags.
strengths: Rare athleticism for a 330-plus-pound tackle
Explosive first step and backfield penetration
Aligns anywhere from nose to 7-technique
weaknesses: Little sack production; limited rush moves
Plays high and gets stalled by double teams

12619.name: Trevor Goosby
12619.summary: Huge, long left tackle who became Texas's starter in 2025 and is regarded as a high-upside tackle prospect. Strong and athletic, but still developing technically.
strengths: Rare size, length and fluidity (6-7, 312)
Heavy hands and strong play strength
Patience and leverage beyond his experience
weaknesses: Vulnerable to jab steps and hesitation moves
12619.notes: is wrong; he is listed at 6-7. First year as a full-time starter was 2025.

12633.name: Luke Reynolds
12633.summary: Top tight end recruit in the 2024 class who was a reserve at Penn State before transferring to Virginia Tech, where he has become a featured target in 2026. Graded in the Day 2 range, with some first-round hype on traits.
strengths: Separates quickly for a 6-4, 250-pound tight end
Dangerous after the catch
Reported 4.5 speed and 38-inch vertical
weaknesses: Run blocking is a clear weakness
Limited big-play production (about 10 yds per catch)
12633.notes: Transferred from Penn State to Virginia Tech for 2026.

12518.name: Eddrick Houston
12518.summary: Former five-star recruit who moved from end to defensive tackle at Ohio State. A rotational interior lineman with modest production who currently grades as a later-round prospect.
strengths: Rare speed for his size
Effective long-arm and bull rush
Can fit multiple fronts
12518.notes: he is now an interior DT listed at about 292-304.

12465.name: Nate Frazier
12465.summary: Compact, explosive back who led Georgia in rushing in 2025. Projects as a Day 2-3 pick; ball security and pass protection decide whether he is a three-down back.
strengths: Burst at the line plus a second gear
Low center of gravity and contact balance
Reliable hands on screens and checkdowns

12516.name: Jaylen McClain
12516.summary: Natural strong safety and reliable tackler who started alongside Caleb Downs in 2025 and now leads Ohio State's secondary. Projections range from the second to the fourth round.
strengths: Sure, reliable tackler
Instinctive and heady in the box
Has added ball production in 2026
weaknesses: Few splash plays in 2025 (no INT or FF)
More strong safety than range free safety
12516.notes: Has 2 INTs through mid-2026 per Ourlads.

12448.name: DJ Lagway
12448.summary: Former five-star quarterback with a big arm who struggled with turnovers as Florida's starter in 2025, then transferred to Baylor. A high-pedigree, inconsistent passer still trying to prove himself.
strengths: Strong arm and explosive playmaking
Big, sturdy frame (6-3, 237)
Elite recruiting pedigree
12448.notes: Transferred from Florida to Baylor in January 2026. PFF lists draft eligibility as 2029, which conflicts with other sources.

12620.name: Kam Franklin
12620.summary: Big, high-motor defensive end who played heavy snaps for Ole Miss in 2025. Viewed as a mid-to-late round prospect.
strengths: High effort and heavy snap count
Productive run defender (69 tackles in 2025)
Big 6-5 frame
weaknesses: Modest sack totals for an edge
12620.notes: Ourlads lists 6-5, 300 and cfbstats 6-5, 290. Sources disagree on class (sophomore vs. junior).

12597.name: Wilkin Formby
12597.summary: Huge offensive tackle who started at right tackle and right guard for Alabama in 2025 before transferring to Texas A&M. Has posted strong pass-blocking grades in 2026 but sits low on draft boards.
strengths: Massive 6-7, 320-plus frame
Elite 2026 pass-blocking grade (PFF)
Tackle-guard versatility
weaknesses: Run blocking grades lag well behind pass pro
12597.notes: Transferred from Alabama to Texas A&M for 2026;

12622.name: Terrance Carter Jr.
12622.summary: Productive receiving tight end who transferred from Louisiana and posted Texas Tech's best TE yardage season in over a decade in 2025. A flex/move option graded in the third-round range.
strengths: Reliable hands; wins in traffic
Strong after the catch
Precise routes; aligns in slot or flex

12580.name: Kade Pieper
12580.summary: Physical, technically sound interior lineman from Iowa's pipeline who started at guard and is projected as a center. Widely ranked the top interior OL for 2027, in the late-first to early-second range.
strengths: Powerful drive blocker in the run game
Quick hands and sound pass protection
Guard/center versatility
weaknesses: Short arms; longer DL can control him
Can be overpowered by big nose tackles

12707.name: Whit Weeks
12707.summary: Undersized, rangy, high-motor linebacker who was first-team All-SEC in 2024. His stock has fallen after limited 2025 production and injury issues; now a Day 3 projection.
strengths: Sideline-to-sideline range and pursuit speed
Quick processor with good run instincts
Effective blitzer and vocal leader
weaknesses: Light for the position; struggles taking on blocks
12707.notes: Broke his fibula in the 2024 Texas Bowl; also listed out for the Oct. 24, 2026 Auburn game. 2025 game count differs by source (8 vs. 13).

12525.name: Antwan Raymond
12525.summary: Canadian-born lead back who broke out with a 1,200-yard season for Rutgers in 2025. Currently viewed as a Day 3 prospect.
strengths: Makes defenders miss in space
Vision and patience to find lanes
Proven volume carrier
weaknesses: Some see him as a change-of-pace back
12525.stats2025: 12 G · 244 car, 1,241 yds, 13 TD; 18 rec, 225 yds, 2 TD
12525.honors: 2025 Jon Cornish Trophy; 2025 second-team All-Big Ten

12684.name: Justice Haynes
12684.summary: Compact, powerful former five-star back who has played at Alabama, Michigan and now Georgia Tech. Was highly efficient at Michigan in 2025 before a foot injury, and grades as a Day 3 prospect.
strengths: Contact balance; runs through arm tackles
Quick cuts and big-play burst
Very efficient in 2025 (7.1 yards per carry)
12684.notes: Alabama (2023-24) to Michigan (2025) to Georgia Tech (2026).

12464.name: Brian Nelson II
12464.summary: Outside cornerback who broke out at North Texas before transferring to NC State, where he has been a starter. Ball production dipped after the move up to the ACC. National draft boards have not yet featured him; he profiles as a Day 3 / priority free agent type for now.
strengths: Proven ball skills: 4 interceptions in 2024 at North Texas
Experienced multi-year starter with special teams value
Solid 6-0, roughly 200-lb frame for the outside
weaknesses: No interceptions since transferring to the ACC
Little national draft buzz so far
12464.notes: Transferred from North Texas to NC State for 2025. Through part of 2026: 35 tkl, 3 PD (Ourlads). ESPN and the school roster list different class years.

12547.name: Ashton Bethel-Roman
12547.summary: Former four-star recruit from the Houston area who is mainly a vertical deep threat in the Aggies' passing game. Started all 13 games in 2025 and averaged over 24 yards per catch. Local coverage calls him a high-upside breakout candidate, but he is still an early-stage draft prospect.
strengths: Explosive downfield producer: 24.6 yards per catch in 2025
Long frame suited to stretching defenses vertically
Already a full-season SEC starter
weaknesses: Low catch volume; route tree still limited
12547.notes: Redshirt freshman in 2025. Needs to stay in school through the 2026 season to be draft-eligible for 2027. Got an honorable mention for the Earl Campbell Tyler Rose weekly award in Nov 2025.

12712.name: Ian Strong
12712.summary: Big-bodied outside receiver who led Rutgers in receiving in 2025, then transferred to Cal for his final season. He has been a steady chain-mover over three Big Ten seasons, with over 1,600 career yards. Projects as a mid-to-late-round size receiver.
strengths: Size and strength at about 6-1, 211 lbs
Consistent producer: 1,668 yards over three Rutgers seasons
Good yards per catch (14.7 in 2025)
weaknesses: Modest touchdown totals for his volume
Has to prove himself in a new offense
12712.notes: Transferred from Rutgers to California in January 2026, so his 2025 stats are from Rutgers.

12548.name: Eli Bowen
12548.summary: Undersized but highly athletic cornerback who has outplayed his three-star recruiting ranking and is viewed as a nickel/slot fit. ESPN's Matt Miller flagged him as a sleeper in the 2027 corner class, and some early mocks have floated a late first-round grade. Top-100 range on most early boards.
strengths: Rare quickness and long speed for the slot
Tight coverage in 2025: 20 catches allowed on 36 targets
Competitive, physical player who quickly earned a role
12548.notes: Younger brother of former Oklahoma safety Peyton Bowen. Sources list his height and weight differently.

12577.name: Cayden Green
12577.summary: Versatile, powerful lineman who started at left guard in 2024, then moved to left tackle for 2025. Widely mocked in Round 1 (ESPN's Jordan Reid had him at No. 21). Evaluators are split on whether his pro home is tackle or guard.
strengths: Has started at both guard and left tackle
Heavy, powerful run blocker
Rated a top-3 tackle in some 2027 rankings
weaknesses: Injuries cost him games in both 2025 and 2026
Some scouts see him as a guard only in the NFL
12577.stats2025: 10-11 starts at LT (missed games with foot injury)
12577.honors: 2025 All-SEC (Mizzou roster says first team; other reports say second team); 2025 preseason All-American
12577.notes: Began his career at Oklahoma, then transferred home to Missouri for 2024. Had a foot injury in 2025 and an undisclosed injury in 2026.

12589.name: Danny Scudero
12589.summary: High-volume receiver who led the FBS in receiving yards at San Jose State in 2025, then transferred to Colorado. He was among the most productive players nationally on deep (20+ yard) targets. His draft stock depends on carrying that output over to the Big 12 after an injury-hit start.
strengths: Elite 2025 production: 88 catches, nearly 1,300 yards
Productive deep threat on 20-plus yard throws
Reliable hands and route volume
weaknesses: Production came against Mountain West competition
Slow, injury-hit start at Colorado in 2026
12589.honors: 2025 First-team All-Mountain West; Biletnikoff Award semifinalist
12589.notes: Transferred Sacramento State to San Jose State to Colorado. Has an ankle injury in 2026 with only 6 catches for 25 yards in 2 games so far. Sources list 1,291 or 1,297 yards for 2025.

12672.name: Carter Smith
12672.summary: Indiana's left tackle and the anchor of its national-title offensive line. PFF ranked him the No. 1 tackle in the 2027 class. He returned for a fifth season, and most projections have him going late first to early second round.
strengths: Polished, experienced blindside protector
Elite 2025 resume: Big Ten OL of the Year
Consistency and technique on a championship line
weaknesses: Coming back from spring 2026 labrum surgery
Average size and length for an NFL left tackle
12672.stats2025: Starting LT for national champion Indiana
12672.honors: 2025 All-American; 2025 Big Ten Offensive Lineman of the Year; 2025 First-team All-Big Ten
12672.notes: Tore his labrum in spring 2026 and had surgery. Some sites still list him as a 2026 draft prospect, but he returned for 2026.

12417.name: Marcus Neal Jr.
12417.summary: Rangy, playmaking safety who was one of Iowa State's leading tacklers before transferring to Penn State. Forecasts range from Round 1 (SI mocked him No. 20) to Day 2. PFF graded him among the better safeties nationally in 2026.
strengths: Active run defender who makes plays behind the line
Good size for the position at about 6-1, 215
Takeaway production: 2 INT in 2025
weaknesses: Only one season of Big Ten tape
Projections vary widely, Round 1 to Day 2
12417.notes: Transferred from Iowa State to Penn State in January 2026. Ranked 32nd of 713 safeties by PFF (82.5) in 2026. PFF lists 2029 draft eligibility, which conflicts with the other sources.

12635.name: Braylon Staley
12635.summary: Productive young receiver who was the SEC's top freshman in 2025, leading a deep Tennessee room in catches. He made big plays in marquee games. He is an underclassman with a high ceiling.
strengths: Immediate high-volume producer as a true freshman
Delivered in big games (2 TD vs. Oklahoma)
Young, with plenty of development runway
12635.honors: 2025 FWAA Freshman All-American; 2025 AP SEC Freshman of the Year
12635.notes: He was a true freshman in 2025, so he would normally not be draft-eligible until 2028 (three years out of high school). His 2027 projection may be invalid.

12630.name: Jamari Johnson
12630.summary: Big, versatile tight end who took over as Oregon's TE1 after Kenyon Sadiq was drafted in the first round. PFF and others rank him at or near the top of the 2027 tight end class, and early mocks put him in the back half of Round 1.
strengths: Traditional in-line blocker who also stretches the seam
Large frame, listed up to 6-6, 245-257
Efficient receiver: 15.9 yards per catch in 2025
weaknesses: Modest career catch volume so far
12630.notes: Transferred from Louisville to Oregon. Returned for 2026 instead of declaring.

12570.name: Kyran Duhon
12570.summary: Undersized edge rusher who earned Freshman All-American notice at UTEP, had a quiet year at Oklahoma State, and is now at Tulsa. Database stats show a strong pass-rush start in 2026. He is a developmental Day 3 type.
strengths: Proven early pass-rush production at UTEP
Quick first step and bend off the edge
6 sacks, 2 FF so far in 2026 (Ourlads)
weaknesses: Little impact in 2025 at Oklahoma State
12570.honors: 2024 Second-team Freshman All-American (The Athletic); 2024 C-USA All-Freshman
12570.notes: Transferred UTEP to Oklahoma State to Tulsa, per Ourlads.

12427.name: Vic Burley
12427.summary: Highly recruited interior defensive lineman whose career has been slowed by knee injuries, and who has been a rotational piece so far. He was expected to step into a bigger role in 2026 after Clemson's tackles left for the NFL. Off-field issues cloud his outlook, and his draft profile rests on traits more than production.
strengths: Big, strong body at about 6-4, 315-320
Former blue-chip recruit with physical tools
Most experienced tackle in Clemson's 2026 rotation
weaknesses: Knee injuries and an August 2026 arrest
12427.notes: Missed his freshman year and six 2024 games with knee injuries. Was arrested in August 2026 on a disorderly conduct charge and suspended indefinitely; he has reportedly returned since. Sources disagree on whether he is a redshirt junior or a fifth-year.

12511.name: Rolijah Hardy
12511.summary: Compact, explosive off-ball linebacker who broke out as a full-time starter during Indiana's run to the 2025 national title. Pairs triple-digit tackles with rare blitz production for an inside linebacker. A preseason All-American heading into 2026.
strengths: Rare blitz production: 8 sacks from off the ball
Instinctive, high-volume tackler (102 in 2025)
Disruptive in the backfield: 15 TFL
weaknesses: Coverage role less proven than his blitzing
12511.honors: 2025 Second-team All-Big Ten; 2025 CFP national champion; 2026 preseason third-team All-American (PFN)
12511.notes: Came to Indiana from the Naval Academy Prep School. Sack totals vary by source (8 to 8.5).

12563.name: Trevor Lauck
12563.summary: Former four-star recruit who became Iowa's starting left tackle in 2025 on a line that won the Joe Moore Award. Known as a tough, physical run blocker. Early mocks have him as a Day 2 tackle prospect.
strengths: Physical, hard-nosed run blocker
Started every game in 2025 at left tackle
Well coached in Iowa's pro-style scheme
weaknesses: Only one season as a starter
Pass protection against elite speed still unproven
12563.stats2025: 13 starts at LT (Joe Moore Award line)
12563.honors: 2025 Third-team All-Big Ten (coaches); 2026 Lombardi Award watch list; Athlon 2026 preseason All-American
12563.notes: Played in only 3 games in 2023-24 before starting in 2025.

12550.name: Cormani McClain
12550.summary: Former elite recruit who started at Colorado and turned his career around at Florida, becoming a starting corner by 2026. Long and lean, with tools that have outpaced his production. Draft outlook is still undefined.
strengths: Long frame at about 6-2
Former top-ranked recruit with high-end traits
One interception in each of the last three seasons
weaknesses: Limited production and inconsistent early career
12550.notes: Transferred from Colorado to Florida after the 2023 season and re-signed with Florida for 2026. Through part of 2026: 27 tkl, 1 INT, 2 PD. No 2027 draft projection was found.

12522.name: Kerry Brown
12522.summary: Productive Minnesota safety who plays downhill like a box safety despite a free-safety build. He was viewed as a mid-round prospect after 2025 but chose to return to school. P.J. Fleck has compared him to past Gopher DBs Antoine Winfield Jr. and Tyler Nubin.
strengths: Physical, downhill run support
Ball production: 2 INT, 6 PD in 2025
Coaches tout his instincts and leadership
12522.notes: Was draft-eligible after 2025 but returned. Reports say he has two seasons of eligibility left, so his class year is unclear.

12543.name: Eugene Wilson III
12543.summary: Quick slot receiver who was a big producer early at Florida before injuries cut short his 2024 and 2025 seasons. He transferred to LSU for 2026 and has been a steady contributor there. He is a mid-to-late-round slot prospect if he stays healthy.
strengths: Quick, shifty slot separator
Over 1,000 career yards at Florida
Versatile underneath target
12543.notes: Transferred from Florida to LSU in January 2026. Ourlads lists 27 rec, 284 yds, 1 TD at LSU so far in 2026. Florida career: 107 rec, 1,043 yds, 10 TD.

12632.name: Jordan Ross
12632.summary: Former five-star, top-ranked edge recruit who was a backup at Tennessee, then transferred to LSU and became a starter in 2026. Long, explosive traits drive his grade more than production does. CBS ranked him No. 37 on an early 2027 top 100, and one CBS mock had him going in Round 1.
strengths: Elite recruiting pedigree and long, explosive frame
Strong 2026 PFF grade (87.2, top 15 among edges)
Still young, with a high ceiling
weaknesses: Little career production: 1.5 career sacks before 2026
Thin tape; needs to add strength
12632.notes: Transferred from Tennessee to LSU in January 2026.

12561.name: Elijah Paige
12561.summary: Tall, long left tackle who started as a redshirt freshman and has been USC's blindside anchor. His 2025 season was cut short by injuries, but his 2026 tape has graded among the best in the nation. Projections range from Day 2 to first-round buzz.
strengths: Prototype length at about 6-7, 320
Elite 2026 PFF grade (83.4, 7th of 619 OTs)
Experienced at left tackle since 2024
12561.notes: Two lower-body injuries in 2025, ending with a knee procedure. Re-signed with USC for 2026.

12701.name: DJ Hicks
12701.summary: Veteran Texas A&M interior lineman who had a career year in 2025 as one of the line's few experienced players. Brings steady disruption from tackle and was named to the Lombardi preseason watch list. Projects as a mid-round rotational DT.
strengths: Disruptive inside: 6.5 TFL, 15 pressures in 2025
Experienced veteran leader
Versatile size, about 6-4, 259-plus
weaknesses: Lighter than typical for a full-time DT
12701.honors: 2026 preseason third-team All-SEC (media); 2026 Lombardi Award watch list
12701.notes: Ourlads shows only partial 2025 tackle numbers.

12716.name: Nyck Harbor
12716.summary: Massive, track-level athlete at receiver who had his best season in 2025, leading South Carolina wideouts in yards. His size-speed combination fuels a wide range of evaluations. Production and polish lag behind his tools.
strengths: Rare size-speed blend at about 6-5, 235
Big-play ability: 20.6 yards per catch in 2025
Ceiling as a vertical X receiver
weaknesses: Route running and hands still developing
12716.notes: Some outlets projected him for the 2026 draft, but he returned for his senior season.

12461.name: Ethan O'Connor
12461.summary: Ball-hawking cornerback who broke out at Washington State in 2024, then came to Miami as one of the top portal defensive backs. His interception production dried up in 2025, though he stayed active against the run. He is a mid-round corner prospect with a lean frame.
strengths: Proven ball skills: 4 INT, 8 PBU in 2024
Active, willing tackler for a corner
Multi-year starter
12461.notes: Transferred from Washington State to Miami in January 2025. Miami's roster listed him as a redshirt sophomore in 2025.

12585.name: Tyson Ruffins
12585.summary: Stout interior lineman who was a standout left guard at Nevada, then started every game for Cal in 2025. Guard-only body type. A late-round / UDFA interior prospect for now.
strengths: Durable: started all 13 games in 2025
Compact, powerful build for guard
Multi-year starting experience at two schools
weaknesses: Short for an NFL lineman at about 6-2
12585.notes: Transferred from Nevada to Cal in December 2024 after flipping from Stanford.

12641.name: Austin Siereveld
12641.summary: Thick, powerful, and versatile Buckeye lineman who started every 2025 game at left tackle, then moved to guard for 2026. Experience at four line spots raises his floor. Mocks range from late Round 1 (Fox: No. 29) to Round 2.
strengths: Versatile: has played four OL positions
Reliable pass protector; 2025 reportedly sackless
Powerful, strong frame at about 6-5, 325
weaknesses: Moving to a new position (guard) in 2026
Lacks ideal tackle movement skills, per some scouts
12641.stats2025: 14 starts at LT, 0 sacks allowed (810 snaps, per one report)
12641.notes: he is listed at 6-5. Moved from left tackle to guard for 2026.

12412.name: Jackson Harris
12412.summary: Big-play outside receiver who broke out at Hawaii in 2025, leading the Mountain West in touchdown catches. He was Lane Kiffin's first portal pickup at LSU and has been productive in the SEC. His deep-ball production gives him mid-round appeal.
strengths: Explosive downfield: 19.7 yards per catch in 2025
Red-zone threat with 12 TD in 2025
Has carried production over to the SEC in 2026
weaknesses: Only one season of high-level production before 2026
12412.honors: 2025 First-team All-Mountain West; 2026 Biletnikoff watch list
12412.notes: Transferred from Hawaii to LSU in January 2026. Wikipedia lists 27 rec, 456 yds, 5 TD for 2026 so far.

12418.name: Chris Cole
12418.summary: Hybrid linebacker who plays inside but was Georgia's most disruptive pass rusher in 2025, leading the team in sacks. Some analysts see a first-round ceiling in 2027. Scouts praise his run defense and tackling but not his man coverage.
strengths: Versatile blitzer and edge rusher from LB
Strong run defender and reliable tackler
Elite 2026 PFF grade (86.2, 17th of 773 LBs)
weaknesses: Only one start in 2025; still finding a fixed role
12418.notes: it should be Georgia. PFF lists 2029 draft eligibility, which conflicts with the other sources.

12690.name: Keon Keeley
12690.summary: Former five-star, No. 1-ranked edge recruit who never broke out in three seasons at Alabama, then returned to Notre Dame (his original commitment) via the 2026 portal. He has a big end / three-tech body. Draft outlook rests on tools and his 2026 breakout.
strengths: Elite recruiting pedigree and size (6-5, 270-282)
Can play big end or slide inside
Strong finish to 2025 at Alabama
weaknesses: Has underachieved relative to his recruiting ranking
12690.notes: Transferred from Alabama to Notre Dame in January 2026. Redshirted in 2023 and has two seasons of eligibility left. Some sources list 16 tackles for 2025.

12723.name: Eric Singleton Jr
12723.summary: Speedy, undersized receiver who led Georgia Tech in receiving yards twice before a less efficient year at Auburn. He moved to Florida for his final season. Projects as a Day 3 slot receiver.
strengths: Speed and separation quickness
Proven volume: 56-58 catches each of the last two years
Experience at three Power-4 programs
weaknesses: Low yards per catch (9.2) at Auburn in 2025
12723.notes: Transferred Georgia Tech to Auburn (2025) to Florida (January 2026).

12675.name: LJ Martin
12675.summary: Big, downhill power back who has led BYU in rushing in each of his three seasons and won Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year in 2025. He came back for his senior year instead of entering the 2026 draft. Draft aggregators put him around the Day 3 range (roughly 130-140 overall).
strengths: Patient runner with good vision and quick feet
Physical inside-zone and gap runner who fits downhill schemes
Proven volume workhorse with a high floor
weaknesses: Pass protection needs work: anchor and angles get beaten by power
Forces fewer missed tackles than his size suggests
Receiving work mostly checkdowns and screens
12675.honors: 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year
12675.notes: Lower-body injury in October 2026, with a reported 4-6 week timeline (missed the Notre Dame game).

12535.name: Teague Anderson
12535.summary: Experienced right tackle who started every game at Utah State in 2024, then transferred to NC State for 2025. There was talk of moving him to left tackle for 2026. He gets little national draft coverage and projects as a late-round or priority free-agent tackle.
strengths: Reliable pass protector: 10 pressures and 2 sacks allowed on 788 snaps in 2024
Gave up only one sack in his first NC State season
Multi-year starter at right tackle with possible left-side flexibility
weaknesses: Recruited as an interior lineman; NFL tackle projection is unproven
Very little draft-media evaluation so far
12535.notes: Name is spelled Teague ANDERSEN in all sources. Transferred from Utah State (Jan. 2025). His father, Jason Andersen, played in the NFL from 1998 to 2002. Ourlads lists him at 6-5, 322.

12592.name: Mason Williams
12592.summary: Two-year starting tight end at Ohio (MAC) who moved up to Ohio State through the transfer portal in January 2026. At Ohio he was a steady possession target with red-zone production. He is a late-round or developmental TE prospect whose stock depends on his 2026 role with the Buckeyes.
strengths: Experienced: 26 starts over two seasons at Ohio
Reliable red-zone target with six career receiving TDs
Recognized early: 2024 FWAA Freshman All-American
weaknesses: Modest career receiving totals (48 catches in three seasons)
12592.notes: Transferred from Ohio to Ohio State in January 2026. Sources disagree on his class year.

12658.name: Bear Alexander
12658.summary: Former five-star interior lineman who has played at Georgia, USC and Oregon. He was a stout 3-technique in Oregon's 2025 playoff run. He skipped the 2026 draft to return for a final season, and scouts see a durable, run-first starter whose pass rush has yet to show up.
strengths: Powerful at the point of attack against the run
Elite recruiting pedigree and a thick interior frame
Durable: played all 15 games in 2025
weaknesses: His power has not turned into pass-rush production (1 sack in 2025)
Scouts question whether his tools carry a high NFL ceiling
12658.notes: Oregon lists him at about 302-316 lbs. Three-school career (Georgia 2022, USC 2023, Oregon 2025-26).

12337.name: Samuel M'Pemba
12337.summary: Former top-10 national recruit (Rivals) who started at Georgia as an outside linebacker and moved to Texas A&M as an edge/defensive end. He hasn't had a breakout season yet, so for now he is a traits-based developmental prospect.
strengths: Elite recruiting pedigree (Rivals No. 10 overall, 2023)
Physically developed frame with experience at edge and linebacker
Attacks the line of scrimmage aggressively
weaknesses: Needs work stacking and shedding blocks
Rushes too upright; below-average chase speed
12337.notes: Transferred from Georgia to Texas A&M. SI reports one sack in 2025; full 2025 totals not found. As a redshirt junior he could return to school rather than enter the 2027 draft.

12333.name: Roderick Kearney
12333.summary: Former four-star recruit who was one of the top interior linemen in his class (recruited as a tackle) and spent 2025 as Florida's backup right guard and center. He was expected to step into a starting role in 2026. He is an early-stage interior prospect whose draft timing is uncertain.
strengths: Can play guard or center
Blue-chip recruiting pedigree (four-star, No. 4 interior OL)
Noted for high football IQ since his redshirt year
12333.notes: Redshirt junior in 2026 with eligibility left, so he may not enter the 2027 draft.

12534.name: Elo Modozie
12534.summary: Productive edge rusher who earned all-conference honors at Army, spent 2025 as a reserve at Georgia, and transferred again to Purdue for 2026 to fill a pass-rush opening. He is a later-round edge prospect who needs a productive final season.
strengths: Proven pass-rush production: 6.5 sacks at Army in 2024
Special teams value: blocked two kicks in 2024
SEC experience from 12 games at Georgia
weaknesses: Small for the edge per listed measurements
Limited role and production at Georgia in 2025
12534.notes: His 2025 Georgia stat totals were not found.

12665.name: Evan Stewart
12665.summary: Former No. 1 receiver recruit and Texas A&M transfer with speed and quickness. He passed on the 2025 draft, then tore his patellar tendon and missed all of 2025. The Athletic ranked him the top senior WR for the 2027 draft, and he led Oregon in receiving early in 2026.
strengths: Rare speed (reportedly laser-timed at 4.36)
Slippery and sudden after the catch
Can line up both inside and outside
weaknesses: Slight frame and play strength; struggles in contested catches
Can have trouble separating in traffic
12665.notes: Missed 2025 after a patellar tendon tear. Through mid-October 2026 he led Oregon with 27 catches, 352 yds, 4 TD, then was ruled out vs. Nebraska. RotoBaller also reported a DUI booking in October 2026.

12724.name: Austin  Romaine
12724.summary: Physical downhill linebacker who was a three-year contributor at Kansas State and transferred to Texas Tech for his final year to replace Jacob Rodriguez. He projects as a mid-round, run-first off-ball linebacker.
strengths: Downhill thumper who is strong against the run
Productive: 184 tackles over three seasons at K-State
Ball skills: two pick-sixes in one 2026 game vs. Sam Houston
weaknesses: Slow change of direction shows up in pursuit
12724.notes: Transferred from Kansas State to Texas Tech for 2026 (one year of eligibility).

12440.name: Owen Chambliss
12440.summary: Productive off-ball linebacker who led San Diego State's top-10 scoring defense in tackles in 2025, then transferred to Nebraska for 2026. PFF grades have been strong early in 2026, and he projects as a Day 3 linebacker.
strengths: High tackle volume: 110 tackles in 2025
Gets into the backfield: 9.5 TFL, 4 sacks
Strong PFF defensive grade (83.5) in 2026
weaknesses: Most production came against Group of Five competition

12626.name: Quinton Martin Jr.
12626.summary: Former four-star back who barely played until he broke out in the 2025 Pinstripe Bowl, when Allen and Singleton opted out. He chose to stay at Penn State and is part of a committee backfield in 2026. He is a long-range prospect and is likely to stay in school past 2027.
strengths: Showed lead-back ability: 101 yds on 20 carries vs. Clemson
Four-star pedigree from western Pennsylvania
Added weight and is developing a receiving role
weaknesses: Very small college sample (no 2025 regular-season carries)
Coaches have challenged him to become bigger and more physical
12626.notes: Redshirt sophomore; technically draft-eligible in 2027 but unlikely to declare. Splitting carries with Carson Hansen and James Peoples in 2026.

12671.name: Josh Hoover
12671.summary: Three-year TCU starter who transferred to defending champion Indiana to replace Fernando Mendoza. He is a cerebral, accurate passer and one of the fastest risers in the 2027 QB class, with some analysts floating a first-round ceiling. Through mid-2026 he had thrown very few interceptions.
strengths: Among the best processors in the 2027 class
Accurate, competitive passer (praised by Curt Cignetti)
Proven production: 3,400+ yards and 29 TD in 2025
12671.notes: Transferred from TCU to Indiana for 2026 (final year of eligibility). Did not play in TCU's 2025 bowl game. Stat snapshots for 2026 differ by source and date.

12551.name: Andrew Sprague
12551.summary: Huge, long tackle (6-7 to 6-8) who started all 12 games at right tackle as a redshirt freshman in 2025 and earned All-Big Ten recognition. He briefly entered the transfer portal, then returned to Michigan. Some outlets list him as a possible 2027 first-rounder if he declares early.
strengths: Massive length and frame
Strong run blocker who moves defenders off the ball
Athletic for his size
weaknesses: Only one season as a starter
Early-entry decision uncertain; could stay in school
12551.notes: Entered the transfer portal after 2025, then withdrew and returned. Outland Trophy watch list in 2026, with a reported position switch. Roster lists 6-7, 310.

12692.name: Luke Montgomery
12692.summary: Ohio State's starting left guard, who started 14 games in 2025 and made second-team All-Big Ten. He passed on the 2026 draft to return for his senior year. Projections range from Day 2 (about No. 70 on one tracker) to first-round talk from teammates.
strengths: Experienced starter: 14 starts in 2025
All-conference level interior blocker
Teammates believe he has first-round potential
weaknesses: Part of a 2025 Ohio State line he says must improve
12692.notes: Returned for his senior season instead of entering the 2026 draft.

12419.name: Will James
12419.summary: Ballhawking defensive back who began his career at Southern Miss and became an all-conference player for Houston in 2025. He can play nickel or outside corner. He is on 2026 preseason watch lists and is an underclassman who may not declare.
strengths: Makes plays on the ball: led Houston with 3 INTs in 2025
Creates turnovers: 2 forced fumbles, 8 PBUs
Can play nickel or boundary corner
12419.notes: Transferred from Southern Miss. Sources disagree on his class (Houston roster says junior, ESPN says sophomore). Nagurski and Bednarik preseason watch lists in 2026.

12420.name: Elija Lofton
12420.summary: Receiving-oriented tight end who played 15 games, with four starts, during Miami's 2025 playoff run and ranked fourth on the team in catches. He is an underclassman whose draft timing depends on a 2026 jump in production.
strengths: Move-TE receiving skills
Red-zone contributor (3 TD in 2025)
Big-game experience during a playoff run
weaknesses: Modest production so far (23 catches in 2025)
Light for an in-line blocking role
12420.notes: Carted off with a lower-body injury in the CFP semifinal and missed the national title game. Underclassman; may not declare for 2027.

12651.name: Gabriel Brownlow-Dindy
12651.summary: Former five-star interior lineman who spent three quiet seasons at Texas A&M, then was a rotational tackle for South Carolina in 2025. He came back for 2026. His NFL case rests on traits and pedigree more than production.
strengths: Five-star pedigree
Prototype interior frame (about 6-3, 310-315)
Rotational SEC experience at two schools
weaknesses: Very little production: no sacks in 2025
Has never been a featured starter
12651.notes: Transferred from Texas A&M (Dec. 2024). listed at 310-315.

12687.name: James Smith
12687.summary: Former blue-chip Alabama defensive tackle who was the top interior lineman in the 2026 transfer portal (247Sports) and joined Ohio State for his final season. He rotates at 3-technique and is a disruptive penetrator with mid-round potential.
strengths: Penetrates into the backfield: 6.5 TFL in 2025
Top portal pedigree (No. 1 interior DL, 247Sports)
Praised by Ohio State DL coach Larry Johnson
weaknesses: Has mostly played a rotational role
12687.notes: Transferred from Alabama to Ohio State in January 2026 with one year of eligibility. One source lists 26 tackles in 2025.

12689.name: Samson Okunlola
12689.summary: Former five-star tackle recruit (nicknamed the 'Pancake Honcho') who developed slowly behind Miami's veteran line, playing guard in 2025. He has taken most of his 2026 snaps at left tackle. He has the tools of a developmental tackle, but his draft timing is uncertain.
strengths: Elite recruiting pedigree (No. 16 overall prospect)
Big frame (about 6-6, 333)
Has played both guard and tackle
weaknesses: Very few snaps early in his career (92 in 2023-24)
Competing with freshman Jackson Cantwell at left tackle
Missed most of his freshman season with an injury
12689.notes: Redshirt junior; may return in 2027. 215 of his first 244 snaps in 2026 came at left tackle.

12667.name: Iapani  Laloulu
12667.summary: Three-year starting center from Honolulu who earned All-America recognition in 2025. The Athletic's Dane Brugler ranked him No. 6 among senior interior linemen for 2027. He is a seasoned, decorated pivot with Day 2 potential.
strengths: Highly experienced three-year starter at center
Decorated: 2025 All-American and All-Big Ten
Played both center and guard early in his career
weaknesses: Shorter frame (about 6-2) likely limits him to center
Few teams value centers early in the draft

12421.name: Rasheem Biles
12421.summary: Rangy playmaking linebacker who was one of the ACC's most productive defenders at Pittsburgh. He was the top linebacker in the transfer portal and moved to Texas for 2026. He projects as a mid-round, run-and-hit linebacker who can blitz.
strengths: Effective blitzer: 17 TFL, 4.5 sacks in 2025
Turnover creator: two pick-sixes, two forced fumbles
Covers ground sideline to sideline

12673.name: Suntarine Perkins
12673.summary: Positionless defender who plays both off-ball linebacker and edge rusher and was a preseason All-American in 2025. CBS and ESPN projected him as a possible 2026 first-rounder, but he returned for his senior season. His size makes him a boom-or-bust NFL projection.
strengths: Can play linebacker or rush off the edge
Disruptive: 4.5 sacks and 3 forced fumbles in 2025
Explosive athlete; scouts call him an NFL draft riser

12628.name: Eddy Pierre-Louis
12628.summary: Young Oklahoma interior lineman who played all 13 games and made six starts at left guard in 2025. He was projected as the starting left guard for 2026. He is a developing guard who will probably stay in school past the 2027 draft.
strengths: Early SEC starting experience (6 starts in 2025)
Earned a starting job by his third year
Played in every 2025 game
weaknesses: Run blocking flagged as an area to improve
Health was the biggest preseason concern for 2026
12628.notes: 2024 signee (former three-star). Sources disagree on his class (roster says junior; others say rSophomore).

12339.name: DJ Hicks
12339.summary: Rotational Texas A&M defensive lineman with few career starts but steady snaps over the past two seasons. He was tabbed as a 2026 breakout candidate and is a late-round or priority free-agent interior prospect.
strengths: Reaches the backfield: 6.5 TFL, 3 sacks in 2025
Two years of SEC rotation experience
Seen as a 2026 breakout candidate
12339.notes: 2025 tackle totals differ by source (Ourlads shows 12 solo).

12686.name: Brendan Sorsby
12686.summary: Productive dual-threat QB who had an All-Big 12 season at Cincinnati in 2025, then transferred to Texas Tech. The NCAA rescinded his eligibility in May 2026 after a gambling investigation, and he left Texas Tech in June. Scouts had seen him as a possible top-two QB before the scandal.
strengths: Dual-threat: 580 rush yds, 9 rush TD in 2025
Takes care of the ball: 5 INT in 2025
Two strong seasons of starting production at Cincinnati
weaknesses: Gambling scandal is a major off-field red flag
12686.stats2025: 12 G · 2,800 pass yds, 27 TD, 5 INT; 580 rush yds, 9 TD
12686.notes: Not playing in 2026. The NCAA rescinded his eligibility (May 2026) over a gambling probe, and he parted ways with Texas Tech (June 2026). The NFL held no 2026 supplemental draft, so he is first eligible in the 2027 draft.

12340.name: Shamurad Umarov
12340.summary: Big Georgia-native lineman and former four-star recruit who stayed patient at Tennessee and earned a starting job in 2025. He has two years of eligibility left, so his draft timing is open. He is a developmental tackle or guard prospect.
strengths: Massive frame (6-7, 321)
Four-star pedigree (chose Tennessee over Georgia, LSU)
Stayed and developed into a starter
weaknesses: Limited starting résumé (first year as starter in 2025)
12340.notes: Has two years of eligibility remaining per Tennessee, so he may not enter the 2027 draft. Some sites list him as a redshirt junior.

12706.name: Joenel Aguero
12706.summary: Former five-star defensive back who started 12 games for Georgia in 2025, then transferred to Ole Miss as an immediate starter at safety. He has a versatile secondary skill set and projects as a mid-to-late-round safety.
strengths: Five-star pedigree and SEC starting experience
Versatile DB who has played several secondary roles
Strong tackling games (career-high 7 vs. Tennessee)
weaknesses: Ejected for targeting in 2026 vs. Florida
12706.notes: Transferred from Georgia to Ole Miss in January 2026.

12517.name: Tamarcus Cooley
12517.summary: Transfer from NC State who became LSU's full-time deep safety in 2025, starting every game and leading the team in snaps. He returned to Baton Rouge for 2026 rather than declaring, and projects as a mid-round rangy safety with ball skills if his production holds.
strengths: Durable every-down starter; team-high 777 snaps in 2025
Ball production dating to NC State (2 INTs in 2024 Military Bowl)
Reliable volume tackler from the back end (~70 tackles)
weaknesses: Limited splash plays in 2025: 2 INTs, 2 PDs
Few dedicated draft-analyst evaluations available yet
12517.notes: Transferred from NC State to LSU before 2025. Sources differ slightly on 2025 tackle total (70-72). Chose to return to LSU for 2026.

12521.name: Cam Cook
12521.summary: High-volume, contact-balanced runner who led the FBS in rushing at Jacksonville State in 2025 before following the portal to West Virginia for his final season. He passed on the 2026 draft and was running for over 900 yards through late October 2026; early draft profiles peg him as a Day 3 back.
strengths: Led FBS with 1,659 rushing yards in 2025
Elusive and tough: credited with 101 forced missed tackles in 2025
Proven workhorse capacity (295 carries)
weaknesses: Bulk of production came against Group of Five competition
Average size for a feature back
12521.stats2025: Jacksonville State · 295 car, 1,659 yds (5.6 avg), 16 TD
12521.notes: Career path TCU -> Jacksonville State -> West Virginia (committed Jan 2026, one year of eligibility). 2026 in progress: 923 yds, 7 TD on 186 carries through Oct 28 per PFF. PFF and NFL Draft Buzz disagree on draft year (2028 vs 2027).

12593.name: Jacory Barney Jr.
12593.summary: Slender, quick slot receiver and return specialist who started all 13 games for Nebraska as a sophomore. His NFL path likely starts as a sub-package receiver who adds value on punt and kick returns.
strengths: Dangerous returner: 12.2 yds per punt return in 2025
Reliable hands; reported no drops on his targets in 2025
Experienced starter with two seasons of steady volume
weaknesses: Modest yards per catch (10.8) as a receiver

12652.name: Jayden Maiava
12652.summary: Pocket-oriented passer with prototypical size who posted one of the nation's most efficient seasons for USC in 2025. Evaluators like his touch, quick release and poise under pressure, but split on whether his arm and decision-making translate; The Ringer ranks him a Day 2 type QB.
strengths: Good touch and trajectory control on intermediate throws
Quick release; stays composed and accurate under pressure
Big frame with enough mobility to extend plays
weaknesses: Arm strength questioned on throws beyond 40 yards
Can take risks with the ball; footwork slips under pressure
12652.notes: Began career at UNLV before transferring to USC. Ringer grade 87/100 (QB10, No. 47 overall) for 2027 class.

12657.name: Joe Brunner
12657.summary: Veteran Big Ten interior lineman who started 24 straight games at Wisconsin, mostly at left guard, before transferring to Indiana for his final year. At IU he has been working at right tackle, and his versatility gives him a likely Day 3 swing-lineman profile.
strengths: Allowed zero sacks in 2025 per reports
Experienced: 24 consecutive starts at Wisconsin
Versatile across guard and tackle spots
weaknesses: Still learning tackle after a career mostly at guard
Limited national scouting coverage so far
12657.notes: he transferred to Indiana in Jan 2026 after weighing the 2026 draft. Moved to right tackle in IU fall camp.

12714.name: Dezz Ricks
12714.summary: Former five-star IMG Academy recruit who started at Alabama and transferred to Texas A&M in 2024. He has the size and pedigree of a long outside corner, but college production has been modest, so his draft stock rides on his 2026 coverage play.
strengths: Five-star pedigree with long outside-corner frame
Best coverage grade among A&M outside corners early in 2026
Multiple seasons of SEC experience
weaknesses: Production has lagged his recruiting profile
12714.notes: Also listed as Desmond Ricks. Alabama (2023) -> Texas A&M (2024-). Re-signed with A&M for 2026 reportedly with eligibility remaining beyond 2026, so his entry into the 2027 draft is uncertain. Sources differ on 2025 PDs (5 vs 6).

12677.name: Mark Fletcher
12677.summary: Big, physical feature back who powered Miami's 2025 playoff run and returned for a senior season instead of entering the draft. Several outlets rank him among the top running backs in the 2027 class thanks to his size and yards-after-contact profile.
strengths: Rare size for a RB (listed 6-2, about 225 lbs)
Breaks first contact; 104 forced missed tackles in 2025 per PFF data
Big-game production: CFP-record 507 postseason rushing yards
weaknesses: Pass protection is an open question
Taller runner who can play upright
12677.notes: Full name Mark Fletcher Jr. Chose to return to Miami for 2026.

12539.name: C.J. Bailey
12539.summary: Tall, live-armed passer who took a big step as a sophomore starter in 2025. Arm talent is his calling card, but inconsistent accuracy and a rough 2026 opener have made his draft stock volatile; he could return to school rather than declare.
strengths: Plus arm strength, including on deep throws
Productive 2025: 25 TD passes against 9 INTs
Mobile enough to punish defenses that lose contain
weaknesses: Shaky start to 2026 season vs. Virginia
12539.stats2025: 13 G · 3,105 pass yds, 25 TD, 9 INT; 215 rush yds, 6 TD

12588.name: Decker DeGraaf
12588.summary: Washington's top receiving tight end, who roughly doubled his catch total as a sophomore in 2025. He's viewed as one of the better tight ends in the Big Ten, though his 2027 draft standing will depend on his junior year.
strengths: Established TE1 with growing target share
Precise route runner for the position
Red-zone production as a freshman (3 TD on 15 catches)
weaknesses: Modest overall production so far (360 yds in 2025)
12588.notes: Underclassman; 2027 declaration not confirmed. Listed 6-4, about 245-249 lbs.

12374.name: PJ Woodland
12374.summary: Physical press-man corner who broke out as a sophomore starter in 2025, lining up both outside and in the slot. With Mansoor Delane gone to the NFL, he is one of LSU's top two corners in 2026.
strengths: Top-10 in SEC in passes defended (11) in 2025
Physical in press man; plays bigger than his size
Versatile: snaps both outside and in the slot
12374.notes: PFF lists his draft eligibility as 2029, which conflicts with his junior status. Treat 2027 eligibility as uncertain.

12636.name: Cam Vaughn
12636.summary: Converted quarterback who led West Virginia in receiving in 2025, then transferred to Miami. Miami dismissed him in August 2026 before the season, and no new team has been reported, so his draft outlook is unclear.
strengths: Led WVU in receiving in 2025
Big-play ability (15.5 yards per catch)
Former QB with a good frame for the position
weaknesses: Still raw as a receiver after the position switch
12636.notes: Followed Rich Rodriguez from Jacksonville State to WVU, transferred to Miami in Dec 2025, and was dismissed in Aug 2026 (no reason given). No 2026 team found.

12344.name: Mike Matthews
12344.summary: Former five-star recruit who broke out as Tennessee's vertical outside receiver in 2025. Beat coverage floats him as a possible riser, but his 2027 standing depends on refining his hands and underneath route work.
strengths: Vertical threat: 15.3 yards per catch in 2025
Five-star pedigree with outside X-receiver profile
Big jump in production from 2024 to 2025
12344.notes: Briefly entered the transfer portal after 2024 but withdrew and stayed at Tennessee. Sources disagree on class (sophomore vs junior).

12428.name: DJ Walker
12428.summary: Productive MAC safety and team captain who started every game for Ohio in 2025. Preseason All-MAC honors mark him as one of the conference's top defensive backs, but he'll need strong testing to rise above a late-round/priority free agent tier.
strengths: Captain and 13-game starter in 2025
Active run defender: 61 tackles, 6 TFL
Ball skills with 2 INTs
12428.honors: 2026 Preseason All-MAC first team (Phil Steele, Athlon)

12664.name: Gabe Powers
12664.summary: Former four-star Ohio State linebacker who transferred to Kansas State for his final two seasons. He was a part-time contributor in 2025 and is a co-leader of the K-State linebacker room in 2026, but he projects as a late-round or undrafted special-teams/depth linebacker.
strengths: Four-star recruiting pedigree from Ohio State
Good size for an off-ball linebacker
Expected special-teams value
12664.notes: he plays linebacker. Transferred from Ohio State to Kansas State in Dec 2024 with two seasons of eligibility.

12631.name: Daniel Akinkunmi
12631.summary: London-born NFL Academy product and the top international recruit in the 2024 class, who can line up anywhere on the line. He has been a reserve at Oklahoma and was projected only to compete for the two-deep in 2026, so he's a long-term developmental prospect, not a 2027 draft candidate.
strengths: Big frame (about 6-5/6-6, 320+ lbs)
Has trained at all five OL positions
Top international recruit in the 2024 class
12631.notes: Underclassman backup; unlikely to declare for the 2027 draft.

12708.name: Raleek Brown
12708.summary: Explosive, compact back who moved back from receiver to running back and broke out at Arizona State in 2025 before transferring to Texas for a final season. His receiving background and big-play speed suit an NFL change-of-pace/third-down role.
strengths: Explosive: 6.1 yards per carry in 2025
Receiving background; 34 catches in 2025
Elusive in space (53 forced missed tackles)
weaknesses: Small frame for a feature back
Only one year of lead-back production
12708.stats2025: Arizona State · 1,141 rush yds, 4 TD; 34 rec, 239 yds, 2 TD
12708.notes: USC -> Arizona State -> Texas (committed Jan 2026 with one more year of eligibility after leaving the draft process).

12715.name: Jamari Lyons
12715.summary: Interior defensive lineman in his fifth year at Florida who came back from a 2024 season-ending ankle injury to start five games in 2025. He has been a rotational body so far, which puts him in the late-round/undrafted range.
strengths: Interior size and power for a rotational role
Regained a starting role after a major ankle injury
Former blue-chip recruit
weaknesses: Limited production: 18 tackles, 1 TFL, 0 sacks in 2025
12715.notes: Missed 2024 after an ankle injury in fall camp. Class designation varies by source (rJunior per UF spring roster).

12342.name: Emmett Mosley V
12342.summary: Sturdy outside receiver who started as a true freshman at Stanford and transferred to Texas in 2025. He showed big-play ability for the Longhorns, but foot surgery and a crowded receiver room have capped his volume.
strengths: Good size (about 6-2, 210 lbs)
Big-play average: 14.6 yards per catch in 2025
Produced early: 48 catches as a Stanford freshman
weaknesses: Foot injury and surgery after 2025 season
12342.notes: Stanford (2024) -> Texas (2025-). Foot injury in the Citrus Bowl; had surgery, expected healthy for 2026. Underclassman; declaration not confirmed.

12475.name: Cam Calhoun
12475.summary: Much-traveled cornerback (Michigan, Utah, Alabama, now Ohio State) whose best season came at Utah in 2024. He was a reserve at Alabama in 2025 and needs a big 2026 in Columbus to get on draft boards.
strengths: Ball skills shown at Utah: 9 PBUs, 1 INT in 2024
Experience in multiple Power 4 defensive schemes
Contributes on special teams
12475.notes: he is on Ohio State's 2026 roster. Path: Michigan (2023) -> Utah (2024) -> Alabama (2025) -> Ohio State (2026).

12353.name: Zach Lutmer
12353.summary: Versatile hybrid defensive back who started every game at Iowa's 'Cash' spot in 2025, covering the slot, playing in the box and blitzing. The Ringer grades him as a top-30 overall prospect and fourth-best corner in the 2027 class, which makes him a likely early-round pick.
strengths: Plays slot, outside, box and deep safety
Strong zone instincts and ball tracking (3 INT in 2025)
Effective blitzer: 5.5 TFL in 2025
weaknesses: Misses too many tackles; inconsistent angles
Lacks top recovery speed in isolated coverage
12353.stats2025: 13 GS · 71 tkl, 5.5 TFL, 1 sack, 3 INT (1 TD), 7 PBU
12353.honors: 2025 Second-team All-Big Ten; Iowa defensive MVP (2025)
12353.notes: The Ringer classifies him as CB, and Iowa uses him in a hybrid 'Cash' role. On 2026 Nagurski and Lott IMPACT watch lists.

12385.name: Steve Angeli
12385.summary: Former Notre Dame backup who won Syracuse's starting job in 2025 and was playing efficiently before tearing his Achilles in late September. He returned as the starter in 2026 and threw three TDs in the opener, putting him in the late-round/undrafted QB range.
strengths: Efficient in 2025: 10 TD, 2 INT in four starts
Experienced in two Power 4 systems
Came back on schedule from an Achilles tear
weaknesses: Small sample as a college starter
Achilles tear in 2025 raises medical questions
12385.honors: 2026 Comeback Player of the Year watch list
12385.notes: Notre Dame transfer. Torn left Achilles vs. Clemson (Sept 2025), out for the season; returned for 2026. Exact eligibility class not confirmed.

12387.name: Que'Sean Brown
12387.summary: Undersized, quick slot receiver who was Duke's leading volume target in 2025, then transferred to Virginia Tech for 2026. His size limits him to a slot/return role at the next level.
strengths: Proven volume: 64 catches in 2025
Quickness to win from the slot
Reliable production across 14 games
12387.notes: he committed to Virginia Tech in Jan 2026.

12653.name: Addison Nichols
12653.summary: Former four-star interior lineman who has played center and guard across stops at Tennessee, Arkansas and SMU. He started every game at right guard for SMU in 2025 and is among the top returning interior linemen, a likely Day 3 pick with center/guard flexibility.
strengths: Center/guard versatility (started at C for Arkansas, RG at SMU)
Big, powerful frame (listed around 6-5, 320+ lbs)
Started all 13 games in 2025

12537.name: Jordan Napier
12537.summary: San Diego State's top receiver, who built on a 2024 breakout before a knee injury ended his 2025 season in mid-November. He returned in 2026 wearing a brace, and he projects as a late-round/priority free agent pending health and testing.
strengths: Go-to target: led SDSU receivers two straight years
Biletnikoff watch list recognition
Two straight seasons of 40-plus catches
weaknesses: Modest efficiency and only 2 TD in 2025
12537.notes: Season-ending knee injury vs. Boise State on Nov 15, 2025; returned for 2026 fall camp in a brace.
